title: Architectural pattern selection
task_statement: Select the least autonomous pattern that meets the task constraints. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Tool-use loop in application code
components.first_principle: The model asks for a tool call, and the application runs the tool and returns the result.
steps: Define each tool with a name, a description, and an input schema.
Send the request with the tools array and the user message.
Read stop_reason, and run each requested tool in code when it is tool_use.
Return each result in a tool_result block on the next request.
Exit the loop on end_turn, and handle any other stop reason in code.
pros: Your code runs every tool, so your code controls each side effect.
A tool schema enforces the shape of each input.
Fixed steps stay in code, not in a model plan. (Inference)
cons: Every tool call is at least one extra round trip.
The loop needs stop reason handling in code. (Inference)
The model chooses tools, so each tool description must be precise. (Inference)
use_when: The model needs fresh or external data from a tool.
The task needs one judgment and one side effect in your system. (Inference)
A tool input must follow a schema.
do_not_use_when: The model can answer from training alone.
A tool call would add more delay than the answer needs. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep the loop short, with one round trip for each tool call.
constraints.combination: Run independent, read-only tools in parallel.

constraints.choice: Count one model call for each loop turn. (Inference)
Scope each tool to the data the task needs. (Inference)
Log each tool name, its input, and the size of its result. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.3. Expect a task with one judgment step and a side effect. The credited answer keeps the steps in application code and calls the model at the judgment step. (Inference)
components.trap: A full agent for one judgment step. The agent adds planning overhead that the task does not need. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use a tool-use loop when the steps are known, and the model only chooses tools.
components.exam_tip: If the stem names one tool call and a fixed sequence, pick application code over an agent. (Inference)

key_facts.text: Tool use does not fit when the model can answer from training alone.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Every tool call is at least one extra round trip.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Independent, read-only tool operations are usually safe to run in parallel for lower latency.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Agent loop with model-planned steps
components.first_principle: An agent plans its own steps and calls tools until the task is complete or a limit stops the run.
steps: Give the agent a goal and the tools it can use.
The agent chooses the next tool call from the goal and the results so far.
The agent runtime or your application runs each tool and returns the result.
The loop continues until the agent stops or a limit applies.
Set a session budget so that the session pauses when its list cost reaches the cap.
pros: The agent handles steps that are unknown before the run starts.
The agent can change its plan when a tool result changes the picture.
The Agent SDK gives an agent built-in tools, an agent loop, and context management.
cons: Each run can take a different path. (Inference)
Every agent in a run uses tokens, so cost rises with the run length.
Traces show a plan that the team did not write. (Inference)
use_when: The steps depend on results that cannot be listed in advance.
The task is open research with unknown sources and steps. (Inference)
A person checks the result before any side effect happens. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The steps are fixed, and a rule covers every case. (Inference)
The error cost is high, and no check can verify each step. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a session budget that caps the spend of the run.
constraints.combination: Set a lower budget for runs with fixed steps. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Limit the agent to the tools and agents that you list.
constraints.combination: Use Managed Agents permission policies to make server-executed tools wait for approval.

constraints.choice: Review the run traces and the session events after each run. (Inference)
Write the system prompt with clear rules for when to stop. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.3. Expect a task whose steps are unknown until the run starts. The credited answer uses an agent loop with a spend cap and a tool list. (Inference)
components.trap: An agent loop for a task with fixed steps. The agent makes more model calls and varies from run to run with no gain. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Choose the least autonomous pattern that covers every step the task needs.
components.exam_tip: If the steps are known in advance, pick code with a model call at the judgment step, not an agent. (Inference)

key_facts.text: An agent is an application that plans its own steps and calls tools to complete a task.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Every agent in a run uses tokens, so a session budget caps the session spend, runs included.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A session budget stops new model requests when the list cost reaches the budget.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: On Claude Platform on AWS, a Managed Agents session runs without user events for up to 6 hours before it needs reauthentication.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Steps known before the run?} -->|Yes| B{One judgment needed?}
  A -->|No| C[Agent loop with spend cap]
  B -->|No| D[Code with no model call]
  B -->|Yes| E[Tool-use loop in application code]
  E --> F{Many independent parts?}
  F -->|Yes| G[Split into parallel pieces]
  F -->|No| H[Keep one tool-use loop]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  T[Task] --> S{Steps known}
  S -->|Yes| C[Code path]
  C --> J{Judgment step}
  J -->|Yes| L[Model call with tools]
  S -->|No| A[Agent loop]
  A --> B[Spend cap]
  A --> R[Tool list]

patterns.wording: a fixed task with steps known in advance
patterns.answer_type: code with a model call at the judgment step
patterns.rule: Keep the steps in code. Call the model only where judgment is needed.
traps: Model plan for a fixed sequence

patterns.wording: steps unknown until the run starts
patterns.answer_type: agent loop with a spend cap
patterns.rule: Use an agent loop when the plan depends on results. Add a budget.
traps: Fixed code path that cannot adapt
Agent with no budget and no tool list

patterns.wording: one judgment step with a side effect
patterns.rule: Define one tool set. Run each tool in your code.
traps: Full agent for one judgment step
Side effect with no tool result check
